title: SAMPA Emerging Practice Monthly No. 1 (October 2026)
kicker: SAMPA Emerging Practice Monthly · No. 1 · October 2026
headline: Long-acting injectable bup for people transferring from methadone
summary: Welcome to the first SAMPA Emerging Practice Monthly: recent research on an emerging addiction practice, with plain-language summaries and links to the original sources. In this issue: a new outpatient case series, a systematic review of transfer strategies, two inpatient approaches and a cautionary case on moving people from methadone to long-acting injectable bup.

items.headline: Going straight from methadone to injectable bup in clinic: 15-patient case series, 93% got a monthly injection
items.outlet: Liauw et al. · Journal of Addiction Medicine
items.summary: In a retrospective study at one academic health system, 15 people in methadone treatment with opioid use disorder in remission requested a direct-to-inject transition in 2025, starting with weekly injectable bup; 93% went on to receive a monthly extended-release injection and 67% were still on bup at 90 days. Mean methadone dose was 71.5 mg (range 24 to 120), and 33% reported moderate or severe discomfort, all at methadone doses of 95 mg or more, with symptoms responsive to anxiolytics. The sample is small and uncontrolled, but PAs may want to plan for more withdrawal-related discomfort when transitioning people from higher methadone doses.

items.headline: Systematic review: methadone-to-bup transfer protocols vary widely, and lower methadone doses predict success
items.outlet: Lintzeris et al. · Journal of Addiction Medicine
items.summary: The authors searched six databases and trial registries for studies of transfer from methadone to sublingual bup and found 18 studies, with extremely varied transfer protocols. Most reported successful transfer, even from high methadone doses, though a lower pre-transfer methadone dose was significantly associated with higher success, and precipitated withdrawal was not reported often. Few studies allowed head-to-head comparison of approaches, so PAs should treat guidelines as guidance rather than fixed protocols and use clinical judgment with each patient.

items.headline: Hospital case: high-dose bup initiation moves a patient off methadone 180 mg, later onto monthly long-acting bup
items.outlet: Schnipke et al. · Substance Use & Addiction Journal
items.summary: The authors reviewed the literature on high-dose bup initiation and found no prior reports of successful transition from methadone doses as high as 180 mg, then described one hospitalized patient transitioned from 180 mg with support from adjunctive medications. The patient stabilized within one week on 32 mg of daily bup and later on monthly long-acting bup. This single case suggests inpatient high-dose initiation may be feasible for people on high-dose methadone where close monitoring is available, but it does not establish safety or generalizability.

items.headline: Low-dose inpatient transitions from methadone and other full agonists onto long-acting bup were well tolerated in 7 hospitalized patients
items.outlet: Seval et al. · Journal of Addiction Medicine
items.summary: Within the COMMIT randomized trial of long-acting bup for people with opioid use disorder hospitalized with serious infections, the authors describe seven participants on full agonist opioids, including methadone, who were moved to bup with low-dose (microdosing) strategies before a long-acting injection. Starting buccal doses were 225 to 300 µg three times on day 1; all transitions were well tolerated, with an average of 7.5 days (range 5 to 10) to the injection despite significant pain and frequent surgery. It is a small case series, but it shows PAs a way to give long-acting bup before discharge, when overdose risk is high.

items.headline: Cautionary case: a rapid switch from methadone 140 mg to extended-release bup ended in withdrawal and a return to methadone
items.outlet: Jhawar and Menard-Okoroike · Mental Health Clinician
items.summary: A 43-year-old man stable on methadone 140 mg daily was moved to bup using transdermal patches and a methadone cut of about half on day 3, then received a 300 mg extended-release injection on day 5; he developed significant withdrawal, was hospitalized, reported repeated returns to opioid use and suicidal ideation, and was restarted on methadone. The authors attribute the failure to the high pre-transition methadone dose, the rapid transition and patient reluctance, and note that tapering methadone to 30 to 40 mg before transition is commonly recommended. A single case cannot show how often this happens, but it is a reminder for PAs to be cautious with rapid cross-titration from high-dose methadone.
